title: Under birth-site depletion the Marangoni trait sets how fast a rod leaves, not how far it goes per cycle: alone, mar-60 rods move 1.5-2x faster and divide sooner, but cover the same 3-3.7 own lengths per cycle as mar 40 (2 seeds), so the depletion step levels the heritable trait's effect on the capability
summary: Single-kind populations (all mar 40 or all mar 60, mutation off) of loop 2's world. With depletion discs at split sites (seeds 620, 621): median D 3.69 vs 3.17 and 2.92 vs 3.07 own rod lengths, path speed 0.25 vs 0.39 and 0.16 vs 0.33, cycle 338 vs 305 and 470 vs 322 t, M passers 8/10 vs 9/15 and 5/11 vs 7/14, vanishings per split alike. With sink discs only (seed 620) mar 60 goes farther per cycle (2.42 vs 1.59) but loses more bodies per split (1.35 vs 0.86). A fixed-radius depletion pays distance by fixing it, so there is no heritable variation in the capability for selection to act on; a supply that grows with distance from the birth site is the next candidate.

finding.operator: birth-site depletion discs (trait-blind) on single-kind Marangoni rod populations
finding.control: same world without depletion (sink discs only), seed 620; paired single-kind arms on seeds 620-621
finding.result: median D mar 40 vs mar 60 with depletion 3.69/3.17 (620), 2.92/3.07 (621); without depletion 1.59/2.42 (620). Cycle with depletion 338/305, 470/322 t; path speed 0.25/0.39, 0.16/0.33. Vanishings per split with depletion 0.85/0.89, 1.29/1.22; without 0.86/1.35.
